title: States of matter
description: A child moves one substance among solid, liquid, and gas and compares how the particles are arranged.
learningObjectives: Explain how particles are arranged in a solid, a liquid, and a gas, and compare the three.

params.description: Which state the substance starts in.

events.name: state_changed
events.description: The child moved the substance from one state to another.

events.name: particle_observed
events.description: The child looked at how close the particles are in that state.

tutorGuide.intro: Particles stay put, slide, or fly. The state is the difference.
steps: Look at the state the sample starts in.
Watch the particles, then compare the three jars.
observationPrompts: Where are the particles closest together?
What do the gas particles do that the solid particles do not?

misconceptions.belief: A solid is one hard piece with nothing inside.
misconceptions.response: A solid is many tiny particles. They are packed in place and only jiggle.

misconceptions.belief: Gas is empty, so it has no particles.
misconceptions.response: A gas is particles too. They are far apart and moving, so the jar looks mostly empty.

hints: Start with the solid. The particles sit in rows.
Liquid particles stay close and slide. Gas particles fly far apart.

successCriteria.description: Moved the substance from one state to another
Noticed how the particles are spaced in the chosen state

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: Three buttons show a solid, a liquid, and a gas. The picture and the sentence change to match the particles.
